questions.question: Ratha Jatra, the festival of Chariots of Lord Jagannatha is celebrated every year in ______.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Puri, Odisha**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Origins and Significance:**

 
• **Ratha Jatra,** also known as the **Chariot Festival,** is a significant event in** Hinduism.**
 
• It is dedicated to** Lord Jagannatha, a form of Lord Vishnu,** and his siblings, **Lord Balabhadra and Goddess Subhadra.**
 
• The festival symbolizes **Lord Jagannatha's annual visit to his birthplace, the Gundicha Temple.**

**Location and Time:**

 
• The festival takes place in **Puri, a city in the Indian state of Odisha.**
 
• It is usually held in the month of Ashadha, which falls in June or July according to the **Gregorian calendar.**

**Chariot Construction and Procession:**

 
• Three chariots are constructed for the festival, each representing one of the deities - **Lord Jagannatha, Lord Balabhadra, and Goddess Subhadra.**
 
• These chariots are pulled by devotees in a grand procession from the main Jagannatha temple to the **Gundicha Temple.**

**Rituals and Celebrations: **

 
• The festival lasts for **nine days.**
 
• The deities are bathed and adorned with new clothes and jewelry.
 
• They are then placed on the chariots for the procession.
 
• Upon reaching the Gundicha Temple, they stay there for seven days and then return to the **main temple, marking the end of the festival.**

**Global Recognition:**

 
• While the festival has its roots in Puri, it is now celebrated globally by the **International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) **and other Hindu communities around the world.
 
• The festival is known for its display of devotion and the **vibrant cultural heritage of Odisha.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the production possibility frontier?

I. It gives the combinations between two goods that can be produced when the resources of the economy are fully utilised.

II. It illustrates the production possibilities of the economy.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Both I and II**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Production Possibility Frontier (PPF):**

**Statement 1:**

 
• The **PPF** does indeed illustrate the combinations of **two goods or services** that can be produced when the resources of the economy are **fully and efficiently utilized.**
 
• It shows the trade-off between the production of **one good and the production of another, **assuming all resources are used to their **fullest potential.**

**Statement 2:**

 
• The PPF also illustrates the **production possibilities of the economy.**
 
• It shows the maximum possible output combinations of two goods or services an economy can achieve when all resources are **fully and efficiently employed.**
 
• The **PPF **is typically depicted as a downward-sloping curve, with **one good on each axis.**
 
• Points along the curve represent efficient production levels, while points below the curve indicate **inefficiency **and points above the curve are unattainable with current resources and technology.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a crop as classified in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​**Nisha**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

 
• India has three cropping seasons — Rabi, Kharif and Zaid.
 
• Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December and harvested in summer from April to June.
 
 
• Some of the important rabi crops are wheat, barley, peas, gram and mustard.
 
• Though these crops are grown in large parts of India, states from the north and north-western parts such as Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh are important for the production of wheat and other rabi crops.
 
• Availability of precipitation during winter months due to the western temperate cyclones helps in the success of these crops.
 
• However, the success of the green revolution in Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh and parts of Rajasthan has also been an important factor in the growth of the abovementioned rabi crops.
 
 
 
• Kharif crops are grown with the onset of monsoon in different parts of the country and these are harvested in September-October.
 
 
• Important crops grown during this season are Paddy, Maize, Jowar, Bajra, Tur(Arhar), Moong, Urad, Cotton, Jute, Groundnut and Soybean.* Hence, Groundnut is the correct answer.*
 
• Some of the most important rice-growing regions are Assam, West Bengal, coastal regions of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Maharashtra, particularly the (Konkan coast) along with Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
• Recently, paddy has also become an important crop of Punjab and Haryana.
 
• In states like Assam, West Bengal and Odisha, three crops of paddy are grown in a year. These are Aus, Aman and Boro.
 
 
 
• In between the rabi and the Kharif seasons, there is a short season during the summer months known as the Zaid season.
 
 
• Some of the crops produced during ‘Zaid’ are watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder crops.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding river Ganga is correct?

options.text: Ghaghara is a tributary coming from peninsular uplands.
Yamuna is a right bank tributary meets the Ganga at Allahabad.
The length of the Ganga is over 5000 km.
Betwa is a tributary of river Ganga rising from the Himalayas.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Yamuna is a right bank tributary meets the Ganga at Allahabad.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**River Ganga

__
 
• It originates in the Himalaya Mountains at Gomukh, the terminus of the Gongotri Glacier. Here, it is known as the Bhagirathi.
 
• It cuts through the Central and the Lesser Himalayas in narrow gorges.
 
• At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda; hereafter, it is known as the Ganga.
 
• The river has a length of 2,525 km. *(Option 3 Incorrect)__*
 
• It is shared by Uttarakhand (110 km) and Uttar Pradesh (1,450 km), Bihar (445 km) and West Bengal (520 km).
 
• The river finally discharges itself into the Bay of Bengal near Sagar Island.
 
• Left tributaries: Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Burhi Gandak, Koshi, Mahananda, Ramganga, Garra.
 
• Right tributaries: Yamuna, Sone, Punpun, Damodar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**Yamuna:

__
 
• ​Originates from Yamunotri Glacier.
 
• Passes from states- Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi.
 
• Merge in Ganga at Praygraj(Allahabad). ***(Option 2 correct)**__*
 
• The Yamuna is the second-largest tributary river of the Ganga and the longest tributary.
 
• Left tributaries of Yamuna are Tons, Hindon, Hanuman Ganga, Sasur, Khaderi.
 
• Right tributaries of Yamuna are Giri, Baghain, Chambal, Betwa, Sindh, Ken.
 
• Length of river 1,376 km. 

**River Ghaghara :**

__
 
• Ghaghara River is also called the Gogra, Ghaghara or Ghagra, Nepali Kauriala or Manchu or the Karnali.
 
• However, the literal meaning of the river is ' holy water from the sacred mountain',
 
• The term Karnali also means "Turquoise River" and is a transboundary perennial river that originates on the Tibetan plateau. *(Option 1 Incorrect)__*
 
• The Karnali is called K'ung-ch'iao Ho in Chinese.
 
• This river near Manasarovar cuts through the Himalayas in Nepal on its way to the convergence with the Sarda River at Brahmaghat in India where it forms the Ghaghara River.
 
• The Ghaghara River is a major left-bank tributary of the Ganges.
 
• It is the longest and largest river in Nepal with a length of around 507 km and one of the largest affluent of the Ganges.

River Betwa:

__
 
• It originates from the Vindhyachal Ranges of Raisen district in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Betwa is an important tributary of the river Yamuna. ***(Option 4 Incorrect)**__*
 
• The length of the river Betwa is around 590 Km.
 
• Important cities on the bank of the river Betwa are Vidisha, Sanchi, and Orcchaa.
 
• Raj Ghat Dam is situated on the river Betwa.
 
• Ken-Betwa river interlinking project is the proposed project to transfer the surplus water from River Ken to Betwa in order to meet the water needs of the drought-prone Bundelkhand Region of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian constitution states that “The Council of States shall, as soon as may be, choose a member of the Council to be Deputy Chairman thereof and, so often as the office of Deputy Chairman becomes vacant, the Council shall choose another member to be Deputy Chairman thereof.”?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Article 89**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Vice-President** is the **ex-officio chairman of the Rajya Sabha.**
 
• The** Vice-President as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** is the unchallenged guardian of the eminence and dignity of the House.
 
• **Article 64:** The Vice-President shall be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States and shall not hold any other office of profit. 
 
• **Article 89:** of the Constitution provides provision for the Chairman (Vice-President of India) and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Power and Functions:
 
• The **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is empowered to adjourn the House or to suspend its sitting in the event of the absence of a quorum.**
 
• The 10th Schedule of the Constitution empowers the Chairman to determine the question as to **disqualification of a member of the Rajya Sabha on the ground of defection;**
 
• The **Chairman's consent** is needed to raise a **question of breach of privilege in the House.**
 
• Parliamentary Committees, regardless of whether set up by the Chairman or by the House, work under the direction of the Chairman.
 
• He nominates members to different **Standing Committees** and **Department-related Parliamentary Committees.**
 
• He is the Chairman of the **Business Advisory Committee, the Rules Committee, and the General Purposes Committee.**
 
• It is the duty of the Chairman to interpret the Constitution and rules so far as matters in or relating to the House are concerned, and no one can enter into any argument or controversy with the Chairman over such interpretation.
 
• He can only be removed as the **chairman of Rajya Sabha **when he is removed from the **office of Vice-President of India.**
 
• While the resolution is in effect for the removal of Vice-President, he cannot preside over the house as chairman, although he can be part of the house.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Article 14: 

 
• The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India, on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

**Article 377: **

 
• **States about the Provision as to comptroller and auditor general of India.**

**Article 370**:

 
• Article 370 of the Indian constitution gave special status to Jammu and Kashmir which has been the subject of a dispute between India, Pakistan, and China since 1947.
 
• Article 370 was drafted in Part XXI of the Indian constitution titled "Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions".
 
• Clause 3 of Article 370 empowers the president to declare the article as inoperative.
 
• Instead of scrapping Article 370, the government used the power given by the same Article to the President to make the provision ineffective.
 
• Scrapping of Article 370 would, otherwise, require a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
 
• But by invoking Article 370(3), the government has cleverly bypassed the amendment route.

questions.question: Speed of ______ printer is measured in characters per second (CPS).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dot Matrix

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

Print resolution is measured as the number of Dots Per Inch (dpi).

 
• ​It can be said that Resolution (in terms of print) is a measure of the number of dots that a device can put in one square inch of page space.
 
• The higher the dot density, the higher the resolution of the print or scan.
 
• A printer with 600 DPI is a printer that prints 600 x 600 per square inch or 360,000 dots per inch.
 
• Increasing the DPI will make the size of the printed image smaller while decreasing the DPI will make the size of the printed image larger.

 

 
• Characters-per-second (cps) is a unit of measure used to describe the speed of dot-matrix and daisy-wheel printers.
 
• Lines-Per-Minute (LPM) is the number of lines of text a printer is capable of producing in one minute. It is affected by factors such as text size, resolution, and colour.
 
• Pages per minute (PPM) is a printer speed measurement standard. It is the measurement standard for how fast a printer can print a standardized page.

questions.question: Tropical grasslands of Brazil are known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Campos**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tropical Grasslands:

 
 
• These are the grasslands that are located in the tropical zones and in the interior part of the continents.
 
• 'Campos' in Brazil and 'Llanos' in Venezuela are examples of tropical grasslands.
 
• Campas in Brazil is also called Savanna grasslands. 
 
• These are rich in plant species and are more diverse than forest ecosystems. 
 
• Savanna grasslands lie between **24°S and 35°S, which includes Uruguay and parts of Paraguay, Brazil, and Argentina.**
 
• In these regions, the climate is subtropical and humid and the rainfall is distributed regularly all over the year.
 
 
 
• Hence, from the above-mentioned points, it becomes clear that Compos in Brazil and Llanos in Venezuela are examples of Tropical grasslands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Temperate Grasslands:

 
 
• These are the grasslands that are located in the temperate zone and in the interior part of the continent.
 
• 'Downs' in Australia, and 'Steppes' in Europe are examples of temperate grasslands.
 
• The temperate grasslands of North America are called Prairies.
 
• The Temperate grasslands in South America are known as Pampas.
 
 
 
• Tundra: Tundra is a type of biome where tree growth is hindered by low temperatures and short growing seasons.
 
• Mediterranean regions occur between approximately** 30° to 40° north and south latitudes on the west sides of continents.**

questions.question: 1 terabytes per second = ______ bytes per second
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**240**____.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A Terabyte (TB) is a measure of computer storage capacity that is approximately 2 to the 40th power, or 10 to the 12th power, which equals approximately a trillion bytes.
 
• A Terabyte is more precisely defined as 1,024 gigabytes (GB), while a petabyte consists of 1,024 TB.
 
• A tbyte, terabyte, or TB, is equal to 1,099,511,627,776 (240) bytes.
 
• However, the IEC defines a TB as equal to 1,000,000,000,000 (1012) bytes.
 
• 1024 TB = 1 petabyte.
 
• 1 TB = 1024 gigabytes.
 
• The terabyte is a multiple of the unit byte for digital information.
 
• The prefix term was defined for the International System of Units in 1960.

questions.question: Who among the following was a ruler of Shunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Pushyamitra__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Shunga Dynasty

__
 
• It was founded by Pushyamitra. There were ten Shunga rulers. 
 
• Their capital was Patliputra.
 
• Pushyamitra was the commander of the last Mauryan emperor Vrihadratha.
 
• Pushyamitra killed the last emperor Vrihadrata and occupied the whole of Magadha.
 
• The name of the first ruler of the Mauryan dynasty of Magadha was Chandra Gupta Maurya and the name of the last ruler was Vrihadratha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Bindusara 

 
• Bindusara was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and father of the King Ashok.
 
• He ascended the throne in 298 BC after his father. 

 Ashoka

 
• He was the greatest Mauryan ruler; Governor of Taxila and Ujjain previously. His rule extended to the whole of the sub-continent except the extreme south. It also included Afghanistan, Baluchistan, Kashmir, and the valleys of Nepal.
 
• According to Buddhist tradition, Ashoka usurped the throne after killing his 99 brothers and spared Tissa, the youngest one.
 
• Ashoka had himself formally crowned in 269 BC.
 
• Under Ashoka, the Mauryan Empire reached its climax. For the first time, the whole of the sub-continent, leaving out the extreme south, was under imperial control.
 
• Ashoka fought the Kalinga War in 261 BC in the 9th year of his coronation. The king was moved by the massacre in this war and, therefore, abandoned the policy of physical occupation in favor of the policy of cultural conquest. In other words, Bherighosa was replaced by Dhammaghosa.
 
• Ashoka was not an extreme pacifist. He retained Kalinga after his conquest and incorporated it into his empire.
 
• He embraced Buddhism under Upagupta.
 
• He sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to Ceylon as Buddhist missionaries with a sapling of the original peepal tree.

• In 1905, Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal.
 
• At that time Bengal was the biggest province of British India and included **Bihar and Orissa**. 
 
• The British argued for dividing Bengal for reasons of administrative convenience.
 
• The partition of Bengal angered people all over India. All sections of the Congress – the Moderates and the Radicals opposed it.
 
• The struggle that unfolded came to be known as the Swadeshi movement which was strongest in Bengal.
 
• The Swadeshi movement sought to oppose British rule and encourage the ideas of self-help, swadeshi enterprise, national education, and the use of Indian languages.
 
• To fight for swaraj, the radicals advocated mass mobilisation and boycott of British institutions and goods.

Gilbert Elliot, the fourth earl of Minto, was viceroy of India from 1905 to 1910.

 
Minto was born on 9 July 1845, Mayfair, London, United Kingdom.

 
Minto serving as Governor-General of Canada from 1898 to 1904.

 
 
 

 Curzon
 
 
In January 1899 he was appointed Viceroy of India.

 
He has created a Peer of Ireland as Baron Curzon of Kedleston, in the County of Derby, on his appointment.

 
In 1901, he founded the Imperial Cadet Corps or ICC.

 
Curzon became Assistant Private Secretary to Salisbury in 1885, and in 1886 entered Parliament as Member for Southport in south-west Lancashire

 
 
 

 Chelmsford
 
 
Chelmsford was born on 12 August 1868, London, United Kingdom.

 
Viceroy and Governor-General of India from 4 April 1916 – 2 April 1921.

 
On 9 April 1905, he succeeded to the title of 3rd Baron Chelmsford of Chelmsford upon his father's death and in July 1905 accepted his appointment as the Governor of Queensland in Australia.

 
He was invested as a Knight Grand Cross of the Order of the British Empire on 4 December 1917.

On April 3, 1926, Lord Irwin was appointed 30th Viceroy and Governor-General of India. This was the most tumultuous period for the politics of India.

 
Irwin was a senior British Conservative politician and diplomat of the 1930s.

questions.question: ______ species are the species which are not found after searches of known or likely areas where they may occur.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Extinct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Extinct species: 

 
 
• If we say that any species is extinct we normally mean that the last existing member has died.
 
• Extinction, therefore, becomes a certainty when there are no surviving individuals that can reproduce.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Endangered species:

 
 
• Endangered species are the species which if not protected will become extinct in a short duration of time.
 
• These species are protected and bred in conserved areas like national park sanctuaries.
 
• These species may be at risk due to factors such as habitat loss, poaching, and invasive species. 
 
• They have a very high risk of extinction in the wild but are still present in the wild in a few numbers.
 
 
 
• Endemic species:
 
 
• These are the species whose plants and animal can be found in a particular geographical region and nowhere else in the world.

questions.question: Which part of human brain is responsible for walking in straight line?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The part of the human brain** that is primarily responsible for walking in a **straight line is the cerebellum.**
 
• **The cerebellum is located at the back of the brain, underneath the cerebrum.**
 
• It plays a **crucial role** in coordinating voluntary **movements, including maintaining balance and coordination during walking.**
 
• While other parts of the brain, such as the **motor cortex in the cerebrum**, also contribute to the control of walking, the cerebellum is particularly involved in fine-tuning movements and ensuring smooth, coordinated motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Medulla:** The medulla, also known as the medulla oblongata, is a part of the brainstem located between the pons and the spinal cord.

 
 
• It plays a vital role in controlling several involuntary functions of the body, including breathing, heart rate, blood pressure, and digestion.
 
 
 
• **Cerebrum: **The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and is divided into two hemispheres.
 
 
• It is responsible for many complex functions, including conscious thought, reasoning, sensory processing, motor control, language, and memory.
 
• The cerebrum is involved in higher cognitive functions and is associated with the conscious perception of walking.
 
 
 
• **Pons:** The pons is a region of the brainstem located above the medulla and below the midbrain. It acts as a bridge connecting different parts of the brain.
 
 
• The pons plays a role in relaying signals between the cerebrum and the cerebellum, as well as regulating sleep, breathing, swallowing, and facial movements.

questions.question: Who among the following has been elected as the new President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) in October 2022?

__
 
• Roger Binny : 

 
 
• He is unanimously elected as the 36th president of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on October 18, 2022.

questions.question: Which among the following is a surface-to-surface missile of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Among the surface-to-surface missiles developed by** India, t**he most prominent one is the **Agni series.**
 
• The Agni missiles are a family of medium to intercontinental range ballistic missiles developed by the **Defense Research and Development Organization (DRDO) of India.**
 
• The Agni series includes missiles such as **Agni-I, Agni-II, Agni-III, Agni-IV, and Agni-V, **with varying ranges and capabilities.
 
• These missiles are designed to be launched from land-based platforms and can deliver conventional or nuclear warheads to targets located on land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Javelin missile **is not developed by** India** but is actually a portable** anti-tank missile system** developed by the **United States.**

 
 
• It is a shoulder-fired,** fire-and-forget missile** that can be operated by a single soldier.
 
• **The Javelin system** is designed to** engage and destroy enemy armored vehicles, including tanks, from various ranges and angles.**
 
 
 
• **The AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM)** is an** air-to-air missile primarily developed by the United States.**
 
 
• It is designed for use by fighter aircraft to engage and destroy enemy aircraft at medium to long ranges.
 
• The AMRAAM missile is widely used by the **U.S. Air Force** and has also been exported to numerous countries around the world.
 
 
 
• **The Spike missile is a family of multi-purpose, man-portable, anti-tank guided missiles (ATGM) **developed by the **Israeli company Rafael Advanced Defense Systems.**
 
 
• It is designed to engage and destroy armored **vehicles, including tanks**, as well as other targets such as fortified **positions and helicopters.**
